name: CrowdSec (detection)
description: Security engine that reads Traefik's logs and detects attacks (scans, brute force, known exploits). Detection only here: nothing is blocked until you add a remediation component yourself.

files.content:
# CrowdSec acquisition: which logs to read. Written once at installation; your edits are kept.
# Reads the Traefik container's log through the read-only socket proxy. Traefik must write its access log to
# stdout (accessLog in its static configuration) for HTTP scenarios to see requests.
source: docker
docker_host: tcp://{{service:socket-proxy}}:2375
container_name:
  - {{traefikContainer}}
labels:
  type: traefik

inputs.label: Keep CrowdSec offline (no community blocklist, no signal sharing)
inputs.help: Off: CrowdSec registers with its Central API, shares attack signals and receives the community blocklist.

privileges.explain: A socket proxy on CrowdSec's private network gets the Docker socket read-only and allows only reading containers and their logs (no POST, exec or delete), so CrowdSec can read Traefik's log.

security: Detection only: no bouncer, firewall rule or Traefik middleware is installed, so nothing is blocked. Remediation (for example the Traefik bouncer plugin) is a separate, deliberate step.
The Local API stays on CrowdSec's private network; nothing is published.

notes: No web interface: use cscli (docker compose exec app cscli alerts list) or enroll it in the CrowdSec Console yourself.

limitations: Firewall bouncers (iptables/nftables) cannot protect a Windows host through Docker Desktop; blocking would have to happen in Traefik.
HTTP scenarios need Traefik's access log on its standard output; without it CrowdSec sees only Traefik's own messages.
Behind Docker Desktop, client addresses may appear as the Docker gateway, which limits what CrowdSec can attribute.
manualSetup: Check what it detects: docker compose exec app cscli metrics, and cscli alerts list.
Optional: enable Traefik's access log on standard output so HTTP scenarios apply.
Optional, separately: add a remediation component (for example the Traefik bouncer) once you trust the detections.

update.notes: Hub collections update independently with cscli hub upgrade; the image changes only with a catalog update.

testStatus.notes: Manifest, Compose file set and route validated; not yet installed on a disposable deployment.
